newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans investigate Yemeni kidnapping of bikers.
newsitem.headline: Germans investigate Yemeni kidnapping of bikers.

text.p: Munich prosecutors said on Monday they were investigating the kidnapping of seven German tourists in Yemen this month while they were touring the Arab country on motorbikes.
The prosecutors said the Bavarian state court in Munich had taken over the investigation from Germany's Federal Court of Justice which had overseen police investigations until now.
They said German law was applicable to offences committed against German nationals abroad and they had taken over the case because three of the captives were from the Munich area.

Yemeni tribesmen seized the seven tourists while they were riding through Wadi al-Dabaat, between the southeastern province of Hadramaut and Mahra province on March 3 and held them for nine days on meagre rations.

Two of them fell ill during their ordeal and treated themselves with medicines they had brought from Germany. One had a fever and the other had pain in his knee. They were freed last Wednesday after security forces besieged the area.
Kidnapping is a common ploy in Yemen by tribesmen holding grievances against the government or foreign oil firms.
Dozens of tourists, diplomats and other foreigners have been seized in recent years in Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest countries.
